method: 33 fetches. Web Summit has no public investor listing: https://websummit.com/investors/ is a marketing page ('Join investors at Web Summit') with no list, and https://websummit.com/partners/ shows only testimonials (no partner list). The public speaker listing gives 20 names, then needs login (see brazil-1). So Web Summit's own server-rendered schedule search (https://websummit.com/schedule/search/<term>/page/1/) was read for 17 firm names (kaszek, monashees, canary, valor capital, astella, bossa, domo invest, cubo, btg, atlantico, maya capital, anjos do brasil, sp ventures, inovabra, finep, bradesco, cventures); a hit counts only where the name appears in a speaker's company or the session text. 8 web searches (Portuguese and English, firm names combined) and 6 page reads (DN Brasil, ANBIMA, Mercado e Consumo, Itaú blog, Altss, Startups.com.br's Web Summit Lisboa 2026 tag). 18 firms checked: 2 found (inovabra via a Web Summit speaker; ANBIMA by its own page, an association not an investor), 3 listed only by a third-party aggregator (Itaú Unibanco, FINEP, CVentures), 13 not found. Context: the Brazilian Pavilion's three 'Pitch session' slots (E369, 10 to 12 Nov) are described by Web Summit as pitches 'to a selected audience of European investors', and the 'Brazil Innovation Happy Hour' (10 Nov) connects Brazilian startups with 'international investors': no Brazilian investor is named in either. Invest.Rio and InvestSP (on stage, see brazil-1) are investment promotion agencies, not investors. Press (DN Brasil 2024 list, Mercado e Consumo 29 Oct 2026) names no Brazilian investor for Lisbon. Absence of named Brazilian VCs is the finding; the schedule search covers only people on the programme, not attendees.
